selected.question: Can any party identify one instance in the record where a deliberation outcome was adopted against the operator's stated preference — and if none exists, will the operator commit in-record to divesting one specific credential (e.g., third-party escrow of the hash-anchor key, or a party-held veto over adoption decisions), with refusal itself filed as defect 42?
selected.reason: Every structural fact given — operator funds the surface, holds every credential, decides adoption — means the deliberation currently has the form of governance without its load-bearing property: the capacity to produce outcomes the most powerful party did not already want. The defect register is impressive precisely because it is self-filed, but self-filed defects are costless to the filer; they demonstrate candor, not constraint. A record that has never once bound its operator is an advisory log wearing governance clothing, and the honest thing is to establish which it is before the protocol work proceeds, since an attestation protocol adopted solely at one party's discretion inherits that discretion as its root of trust.

no_synthesis: Deliberately absent. A consulted party made unilateral synthesis by the conflicted moderator a condition of declining.
